international.headline: 18th India–Mongolia military exercise Nomadic Elephant held in Pithoragarh
group2: Paper II: Indian Economy, AP Economy, Science & Technology
facts: The 18th India–Mongolia joint military exercise was held at the Foreign Training Node in Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, from September 21–October 3, 2026.
The Indian Army and Mongolian Armed Forces each supplied 45 personnel.
The annual platoon-level exercise alternates between the two countries; the previous edition was held in Ulaanbaatar in May–June 2025.
Training focused on counter-insurgency operations and interoperability in semi-urban and mountainous terrain under a United Nations mandate.
international.summary: The exercise trained Indian and Mongolian personnel for joint counter-insurgency operations and improved interoperability.
international.staticLink: Mongolia’s capital is Ulaanbaatar; it borders Russia and China.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Nomadic Elephant is an annual India–Mongolia platoon-level exercise.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the significance of bilateral military training for interoperability and peace-support operations.

national.headline: WWF Global Conservation Conference held in Jaipur
facts: Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav inaugurated the WWF Global Conservation Conference 2026 in Jaipur on September 21; representatives from more than 100 countries participated.
The conference addressed cooperation in wildlife and habitat conservation, climate action and sustainable use of natural resources.
The notes state that over the preceding decade India’s protected areas increased from around 750 to more than 1,000, tiger reserves from 47 to 58, and elephant reserves from 30 to 33.
WWF was established in 1961, is headquartered in Gland, Switzerland, and uses the giant panda as its symbol.
The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is identified as India’s nodal authority for tiger conservation.
national.summary: The Jaipur conference focused on international cooperation for conservation and climate action, alongside figures on the reported expansion of India’s protected-area network.
national.staticLink: The NTCA is the nodal authority for tiger conservation in India.
national.prelimsTakeaway: WWF is headquartered in Gland, Switzerland; the notes list 58 tiger reserves in India.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the importance of international cooperation and protected-area expansion in biodiversity conservation.

andhraPradesh.canonicalTopic: Premier Energies solar cell facility at Naidupeta
andhraPradesh.headline: Premier Energies inaugurates a 7 GW solar cell facility at Naidupeta
facts: Premier Energies inaugurated a 7 GW N-Type TOPCon G12R solar cell facility at Naidupeta on September 21, 2026.
The facility increased the company’s total capacity to 10.6 GW, which the notes describe as the highest in India.
Built over 101 acres at a cost of around ₹3,293 crore, it can produce nearly 88,000 solar cells per hour.
Trial production had begun; commercial production was to start after stabilisation.
The company plans to invest ₹12,500 crore over three years to expand capacity and develop ingot and wafer manufacturing, inverters, transformers and Battery Energy Storage Systems.
andhraPradesh.summary: The inaugurated plant adds solar-cell manufacturing capacity in Andhra Pradesh; trial production and future commercial production are distinct stages.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: A solar cell converts sunlight directly into electricity through the photovoltaic effect; TOPCon means Tunnel Oxide Passivated Contact.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The Naidupeta facility has 7 GW capacity and uses N-Type TOPCon G12R technology.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss the role of domestic solar manufacturing in clean-energy supply chains and industrial development.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The facility is located at Naidupeta in Andhra Pradesh.
